mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of reactions both represent double displacement (metathesis) reactions?

options.A: AgNO3(aq) + NaCl(aq) → AgCl(s) + NaNO3(aq) ; Zn(s) + 2HCl(aq) → ZnCl2(aq) + H2(g)
options.B: BaCl2(aq) + K2SO4(aq) → BaSO4(s) + 2KCl(aq) ; AgNO3(aq) + NaCl(aq) → AgCl(s) + NaNO3(aq)
options.C: CaCO3(s) → CaO(s) + CO2(g) ; Na2CO3(aq) + HCl(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H2O(l) + CO2(g)
options.D: Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl2(aq) + H2(g) ; Fe(s) + CuSO4(aq) → FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s)

mcqs.answer: BaCl2(aq) + K2SO4(aq) → BaSO4(s) + 2KCl(aq) ; AgNO3(aq) + NaCl(aq) → AgCl(s) + NaNO3(aq)
mcqs.explanation: Both reactions in option B involve two aqueous ionic compounds exchanging their constituent ions to form new compounds, one of which (BaSO4 or AgCl) is insoluble and precipitates. This is the hallmark of a double displacement (metathesis) reaction. The other options either mix a double displacement with a single displacement, involve decomposition, or are both single displacement reactions.

mcqs.question: In which of the following reactions does a solid precipitate definitely form under standard conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Barium sulfate (BaSO4) is insoluble in water, so when Ba2+ ions meet SO4^2- ions a white solid precipitate forms. The other reactions either produce only soluble ions (A) or gases/water without any solid precipitate.

mcqs.question: Which of the following equations best illustrates a single displacement (replacement) reaction?
mcqs.explanation: In a single displacement reaction an element (zinc) replaces another element (hydrogen) in a compound, producing a new compound (zinc chloride) and a different element (hydrogen gas). Option A is a double displacement, C is decomposition, and D is an acid‑carbonate reaction.

mcqs.question: Which of the following metals will NOT displace copper from CuSO4 solution?
mcqs.explanation: The reactivity series places silver (Ag) below copper, meaning Ag is less reactive and cannot displace Cu^2+ ions from CuSO4. All the other listed metals are above copper and would successfully displace copper ions, depositing copper metal.

mcqs.learning_point: Use metal reactivity to predict displacement
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a single displacement reaction from a double displacement reaction?

options.A: In a single displacement reaction, two compounds exchange ions, whereas in a double displacement reaction, a metal replaces another metal in its compound.
options.B: A single displacement reaction involves an element reacting with a compound, while a double displacement reaction involves two compounds exchanging partners.
options.C: Both single and double displacement reactions always produce a gas.
options.D: Double displacement reactions occur only in aqueous solutions, while single displacement reactions occur only in solid state.

mcqs.answer: A single displacement reaction involves an element reacting with a compound, while a double displacement reaction involves two compounds exchanging partners.
mcqs.explanation: In single displacement (or replacement) reactions, a free element replaces another element in a compound (e.g., Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2). In double displacement (metathesis) reactions, two ionic compounds swap their constituent ions (e.g., AgNO3 + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO3). The other options contain inaccurate statements about the nature of the reactions.

mcqs.question: When aqueous solutions of Na2CO3 and CaCl2 are mixed, which of the following best describes the reaction?

options.A: No reaction occurs because all products are soluble.
options.B: A double displacement reaction occurs forming CaCO3 precipitate and NaCl in solution.
options.C: A single displacement reaction where Na replaces Ca.
options.D: A decomposition of Na2CO3 into Na2O and CO2.

mcqs.answer: A double displacement reaction occurs forming CaCO3 precipitate and NaCl in solution.
mcqs.explanation: Calcium carbonate (CaCO3) is insoluble in water, so when Ca^2+ ions meet CO3^2- ions a white precipitate forms. The remaining ions (Na^+ and Cl^-) stay in solution as NaCl. This is a classic double displacement (metathesis) reaction. Options A, C, and D describe incorrect scenarios.

mcqs.question: In the reaction between lead(II) nitrate solution and potassium iodide solution, which solid is formed as a precipitate?
mcqs.explanation: Lead(II) iodide (PbI2) is poorly soluble in water and precipitates as a bright yellow solid when Pb^2+ ions meet I^- ions. Potassium nitrate, lead nitrate, and potassium iodide remain soluble, so they do not form precipitates.

mcqs.question: A strip of zinc metal is placed into a beaker containing aqueous copper(II) sulfate solution. Which observation best describes what will happen?

options.A: Zinc dissolves and a reddish‑brown solid of copper deposits on the zinc surface.
options.B: No visible change; both substances remain unchanged.
options.C: Copper metal dissolves and zinc ions precipitate as ZnSO4.
options.D: The solution turns blue due to formation of zinc hydroxide.

mcqs.answer: Zinc dissolves and a reddish‑brown solid of copper deposits on the zinc surface.
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper ions from CuSO4. Zinc atoms go into solution as Zn^2+ ions, while Cu^2+ ions gain electrons and deposit as metallic copper, giving a reddish‑brown coating. The other options describe either no reaction or incorrect products.
